title: WeLion New Energy and its semi-solid-state batteries
gist: WeLion New Energy, a Beijing battery maker, focuses on semi-solid-state cells, claiming 360 Wh/kg in a 2023 Nio pack and 824 Wh/kg in a 2025 lab prototype, plus 11 GWh of capacity with 18 GWh more under construction. MIT Technology Review cautions that costs exceed CATL-type lithium-ion cells and cycle-life data on the prototype is undisclosed.

insights.claim: WeLion pursues semi-solid-state cells with a part-liquid, part-solid electrolyte because fully solid-state cells are extremely difficult to manufacture, aiming for higher energy density and better safety than liquid-electrolyte lithium-ion.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: A semi-solid path could reach market faster than all-solid-state while improving on lithium-ion.
insights.quote: Fully solid-state cells are extremely difficult to manufacture, though.
insights.locator: Several companies, including WeLion New Energy

insights.claim: In 2023 WeLion released a pack with Nio at 360 Wh/kg versus about 200 Wh/kg for current lithium-ion packs, giving over 1,000 km range, but only about 200 packs were made due to high production cost.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: The Nio pack proves feasibility but the 200-unit volume shows the cost barrier to mass production.
insights.locator: On that front, they have made steady progress

insights.claim: A WeLion semi-solid-state battery reached 824 Wh/kg in 2025 testing, over three times current lithium-ion, but the company declined to share experimental details and calls the prototype far from commercialization.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Lab density headline is unverified for real-world viability.
insights.locator: WeLion’s engineers made a semi-solid-state battery

insights.claim: WeLion plans a semi-solid-state drone battery at 410 Wh/kg by end of 2026 and its first all-solid-state car battery in 2027 at an expected 400 Wh/kg.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Drone cells are the nearest commercial use; the all-solid-state car cell is a 2027 milestone to monitor.
insights.locator: WeLion plans to bring a new semi-solid-state battery for drones

insights.claim: Two inland cargo ships powered by WeLion batteries are due to launch in October 2026 in Huzhou, each with nearly 4,000 kWh of storage for up to 250 km of range.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Electric inland shipping is an early commercial beachhead for high-density cells.

insights.claim: WeLion has 11 GWh annual manufacturing capacity across four Chinese production bases, with two additional plants totalling 18 GWh under construction.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Planned capacity would more than double WeLion's output, though still small next to larger Chinese battery makers.
insights.locator: Today, WeLion has an annual manufacturing capacity

insights.claim: China's transport sector accounts for around 10% of its CO2 emissions, and emissions from inland waterway vessels are projected to grow about 25% this decade to 18.7 million metric tons by 2030, making electric ships a useful decarbonisation target.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Electrifying inland shipping addresses a fast-growing emissions segment.
insights.locator: China emits more carbon dioxide than any other country

insights.claim: WeLion's semi-solid-state batteries are more expensive than conventional lithium-ion cells from larger Chinese makers such as CATL, and scaling production while competing on cost in a crowded market is its main challenge.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Cost disadvantage versus incumbents limits near-term market share outside premium niches.

insights.claim: Lab energy-density results are hard to translate to real-world use, and key details such as cycle life and capacity degradation of the 2025 cell remain unclear.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Without cycle-life data, the 824 Wh/kg claim cannot support commercial valuation.
insights.locator: And while laboratory tests showing high energy density

insights.claim: WeLion's cofounders include Chen Liquan, a Chinese Academy of Sciences scientist who led development of China's first all-solid-state battery in 1988.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Deep academic pedigree supports technical credibility.
insights.locator: Notable fact: WeLion’s cofounders include Chen Liquan
